title: SaaS exfiltration
overview: Review a cloud application record for a large external share of restricted documents.
prerequisites: Be comfortable reading timestamps and saas audit projection fields.

attack.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
attack.rationale: External sharing can provide a route for exfiltration over a web service. The fixture represents sharing and not confirmed download.

hypothesis: A large share of restricted SaaS data to external recipients warrants checking access grants and delivery.
evidence: Check actor, volume, data classification and destination. Review subsequent access and whether sharing was approved.
false_positive: An approved collaboration or e-discovery export can generate a bulk share event.
tuning: Scope approvals by destination tenant, actor and data policy. Distinguish access granted from access used.
response: Preserve share and access logs, revoke unauthorized links and scope external access or downloads.
prevention: Apply DLP, external sharing policy, data classification and conditional access.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The dataset records a synthetic share summary. External access or data transfer needs separate evidence.

questions.prompt: What establishes that recipients used the share?
options: Access or delivery audit records after the grant
The size of a sharing icon
questions.explanation: An authorization event can precede access or never be used.

options: The first letter of the app name
Data class, destination, actor and volume
questions.explanation: Sensitivity and destination provide context beyond record count.
